diagnostic_evidence.quote: If the data are well-conditioned and the classes are separable, convergence is fast.

issues.failure_explanation: The logistic empirical risk is convex but not strictly convex in general. It is strictly convex only when the data matrix has full column rank. For linearly separable data, which the text itself discusses, the infimum is not attained, so no minimizer exists. Existence and uniqueness do not follow from convexity.

failure_location.quote: This function is smooth and (strictly) \emph{convex}, and therefore its minimization admits a unique minimizer.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that the objective is convex, and that a unique minimizer exists under full column rank and non-separability or with added regularization. Drop the claim of fast convergence for separable classes.
issues.overall_effect: The stated existence and uniqueness of the minimizer, and the associated discussion of fast convergence for separable data, are false as written.
issues.title: Logistic regression claimed strictly convex with a unique minimizer
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of a side remark; nothing downstream depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: Implicitly differentiating the stationarity condition for the inner objective sum_i gamma_i R_i gives d theta*/d gamma_j = -H^{-1} grad R_j, where H is the Hessian of the weighted inner objective. The paper instead writes the Hessian of R_j, so the scalar hypergradient becomes a matrix-valued expression. It also defines H as a gradient, which is a vector and cannot be inverted. The stationarity condition is also stated for R_m rather than the weighted sum.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term by grad_theta R_j(theta*) and define H = grad^2_theta of sum_i gamma_i R_i, applying stationarity to the weighted inner objective.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed 'exact' hypergradient is dimensionally inconsistent and incorrect, as is the stated role of H^{-1}.
issues.title: Hypergradient formula uses Hessian of R_j and defines H as a gradient
issues.why_classification: The correct formula follows from the derivation already indicated, so the fix is a short local correction.

issues.failure_explanation: Theta_k = J J^T/m is m x m and the Gauss-Newton matrix J^T J/m is n x n. They share only their nonzero eigenvalues. If m > n, Theta_k has at least m-n zero eigenvalues even when the Gauss-Newton matrix is full rank. If m < n the reverse holds. So small or zero eigenvalues of Theta do not imply small eigenvalues of H. The claim that flat directions correspond 'exactly' to slow function-space modes also ignores the neglected higher-order Hessian terms.

failure_location.quote: small eigenvalues of $\Theta_k$ imply small eigenvalues of $H(\theta_k)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to the nonzero eigenvalues, noting that the zero eigenvalues differ whenever m differs from n.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed exact correspondence between NTK conditioning and Hessian conditioning is unsupported beyond the nonzero spectra.
issues.title: Zero eigenvalues of the NTK wrongly said to transfer to the Hessian
issues.why_classification: Restricting the claim to the common nonzero spectrum is a short local fix that keeps the intended message.

issues.failure_explanation: For a quadratic, the exact per-step error contraction of GD is max(|1-alpha*lambda_min|, |1-alpha*lambda_max|). This equals (kappa-1)/(kappa+1) only for the optimal constant step alpha = 2/(lambda_max+lambda_min). Counterexample: H = diag(1, eps) with alpha = 0.1. The error in the second coordinate contracts by 1-0.1*eps, which exceeds (1-eps)/(1+eps) for small eps. The bound therefore fails for generic admissible alpha.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound for alpha = 2/(lambda_max+lambda_min), or use the factor max(|1-alpha*lambda_min|, |1-alpha*lambda_max|) for general alpha.
issues.overall_effect: The stated 'classical contraction bound' is false as quantified. The qualitative conclusion that ill-conditioning slows GD still holds.
issues.title: GD contraction factor (kappa-1)/(kappa+1) asserted for every step size in (0,2/lambda_max)
issues.why_classification: A one-line change to the step-size hypothesis or the factor keeps the conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This result tells us that SGD does not converge with a constant step size.
With a fixed learning rate and very small batches, SGD initially makes rapid progress

issues.failure_explanation: The following section does not show this. Its constant-step results leave a variance floor, and a mini-batch gradient is just a stochastic gradient with variance sigma^2/|I|, which is still nonzero for fixed |I| < m. With a fixed step, mini-batch SGD reaches only a neighbourhood, and the paper's own experiment shows stagnation. Convergence needs a decaying step, a growing batch, or the full batch.

failure_location.quote: As we will see in the following section, mini-batch methods can converge with fixed step sizes, whereas SGD typically requires a decreasing step size.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Say that mini-batching reduces the variance floor by a factor of the batch size but still needs decaying steps or growing batches for exact convergence.
issues.overall_effect: The promised contrast between mini-batch and single-sample SGD is not established and conflicts with Theorems 1-2 and the experiment.
issues.title: Claim that mini-batch methods converge with fixed step sizes contradicts the later analysis
issues.why_classification: Rewording the claim to match the later results is enough; no proof is affected.

issues.failure_explanation: The strong-convexity step is displayed with (1-alpha*mu) missing its factor ||theta_k-theta*||^2. The term alpha^2 E_k||grad f_{i_k}(theta_k)||^2 is replaced by alpha_k^2 sigma^2. But E||g||^2 = ||grad f||^2 + sigma^2(theta_k), not sigma^2. The next display then uses a different bound with 2 alpha^2 sigma^2 obtained from variance transfer, so the two lines are inconsistent. The final summation also has an index shift: it bounds E||theta_{k+1}-theta*||^2 with (1-alpha*mu)^k and a sum up to k-1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the faulty line, keep the second moment explicit, apply variance transfer directly, and fix the indices (exponent k+1, sum up to k).
issues.overall_effect: The displayed proof is not a valid derivation as written. The conclusion likely survives through the variance-transfer recursion.
issues.title: Proof of the strongly convex SGD theorem: garbled recursion step replaces second moment by variance
issues.why_classification: The correct recursion is already in the proof, so the repair is local.

issues.failure_explanation: L_f appears in the step size and the bound but is never defined (the smoothness assumption only introduces L_i and L_max). The left side evaluates the gradient at theta-bar_K, which is not defined in this theorem; the minimum over k suggests theta_k. The bound contains Delta_f^star while only Delta_f is defined. The theorem therefore cannot be checked as stated, and the step size and constant depend on an undefined quantity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define L_f (the smoothness constant of f), replace theta-bar_K by theta_k, and use a consistent Delta_f, with the hypotheses of the cited result.
issues.overall_effect: The stated rate and constants cannot be verified or applied, and no proof or source is given.
issues.title: Nonconvex SGD theorem statement uses undefined quantities
issues.why_classification: The fixes are definitional and local, and the cited result supplies the intended content.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem bounds the minimum of E||grad f||^2 by O(1/sqrt(K)). K = O(eps^{-2}) therefore gives a squared norm of order eps, i.e. ||grad f|| of order sqrt(eps). Reaching ||grad f|| <= eps requires K of order eps^{-4}. The prose misstates the complexity by a squaring.

failure_location.quote: This means that we need $\pazocal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ iterations to drive the norm of the gradient below the tolerance $\epsilon$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Say that O(eps^{-2}) iterations give squared-gradient-norm accuracy eps, or that O(eps^{-4}) are needed for ||grad f|| <= eps.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised O(eps^{-2}) complexity for gradient-norm accuracy eps is wrong.
issues.title: Iteration complexity misstated: the bound controls the squared gradient norm
issues.why_classification: Correcting the exponent or the quantity measured is a one-line fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, each collocation point contributes one rank-one matrix

issues.failure_explanation: Weyl's inequality only gives lambda_i(Theta_{m+1}) >= m/(m+1) lambda_i(Theta_m). This lower bound is below lambda_i(Theta_m), so it does not show any increase of lambda_min. Nothing bounds the growth of lambda_max, which can rise by up to ||J_{m+1}||^2/(m+1), so kappa can worsen. The conclusion that kappa improves is asserted 'in practice' without argument. The sum of rank-one terms is also J^T J/m (n x n), which contradicts the earlier definition Theta = J J^T/m (m x m); adding a point there borders the matrix rather than adding a PSD rank-one term.

failure_location.quote: the smallest eigenvalue $\lambda_{\min}(\Theta_m)$ increases sharply, while $\lambda_{\max}(\Theta_m)$ is nearly unaffected.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the matrix consistently as the n x n Gauss-Newton matrix, and weaken the claim to eigenvalue monotonicity. Any claim of improved kappa then needs an additional condition showing the new direction raises lambda_min proportionally more than lambda_max.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that adaptive sampling improves NTK/Hessian conditioning has no valid derivation; only eigenvalue monotonicity up to the scaling m/(m+1) is shown.
issues.title: Weyl-inequality argument does not show adaptive sampling improves conditioning (and mixes up NTK and Gauss-Newton matrix)
issues.why_classification: A contained new argument or a weakened claim is needed, but the section's overall message can survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Most of these points lie in regions where $f(x)$ and $r(x)$ are small, resulting in Jacobians that are nearly collinear.

issues.failure_explanation: For the stated model, J(x) = [2, -2+12x(1-x)]^T. For the five uniform points this gives Theta_5 = [[4, 0.08],[0.08, 0.647]], with eigenvalues about 4.00 and 0.645, so kappa is about 6.2 and not 200. For the seven refined points, Theta_7 = [[4, -0.486],[-0.486, 0.786]], with eigenvalues about 4.07 and 0.71, so kappa is about 5.7 and not 13. The 'improvement' is therefore marginal. J does not depend on f or r, so the explanation that the Jacobians are nearly collinear because f and r are small is also wrong.

failure_location.quote: has eigenvalues $\lambda_{\max}\approx 4.1$ and $\lambda_{\min}\approx 0.02$, yielding a condition number $\kappa(\Theta_5)\!\approx\!200$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the example, or choose a model and points that exhibit the effect, and correct the explanation.
issues.overall_effect: The example does not illustrate the claimed order-of-magnitude conditioning improvement.
issues.title: Poisson example: reported eigenvalues and condition numbers are inconsistent with the stated model
issues.why_classification: The numbers and the explanation must be replaced by a new or recomputed example, though the surrounding text can stay.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In order to take into account a notion of time, they use an exponentially weighted average to give more importance to recent gradients.

issues.failure_explanation: Adam's first and second moments are exponentially decaying averages with weights beta^(k-j), which by construction weight recent gradients more. The claim that Adam avoids giving more importance to recent gradients contradicts both the displayed update and the paper's own description of exponentially weighted averages. The intended contrast is with AdaGrad's uniform accumulation.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, it also avoids giving more importance to the most recent gradients.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the sentence, or say that unlike AdaGrad's uniform sum, Adam's decaying average emphasises recent gradients.
issues.overall_effect: The stated mechanism of Adam relative to AdaGrad is incorrect.
issues.title: Adam claimed not to emphasise recent gradients
issues.why_classification: A single sentence needs rewording and no derivation is affected.

issues.failure_explanation: The compute-and-save step is nested in the conditional k>S, so no pairs are stored for k <= S. The discard step at k>S then removes pairs (s_{k-S}, y_{k-S}) that were never stored. The two-loop recursion, which expects the S most recent pairs, therefore has undefined or missing inputs for roughly the first 2S iterations. The algorithm also never enforces the curvature condition y_k^T s_k > 0 that the text requires for rho_k and positive definiteness.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Always compute and save (s_k, y_k), discard the oldest pair only when memory is full, and require or skip updates unless y_k^T s_k > 0 (for example via a Wolfe line search).
issues.overall_effect: As written, the L-BFGS procedure does not maintain the stated memory of the S most recent secant pairs.
issues.title: L-BFGS algorithm stores secant pairs only inside the 'k>S' branch
issues.why_classification: This is a local restructuring of the pseudocode with a standard safeguard.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the sample-wise objective function becomes $f_i(\theta) = \ell\bigl(h_\theta(M^{-1}x),\, y\bigr)$

issues.failure_explanation: For f_i(theta) = l(h_theta(M^{-1}x), y), the gradient with respect to theta is J_theta(M^{-1}x)^T grad_z l. The matrix M^{-1} acts on the input of h_theta and does not appear as a multiplicative factor on the gradient. It is dimensionally inconsistent (M^{-1} acts on input space, while the Jacobian maps parameter space to output space). The accompanying claim that M^{-1} 'alters both the search direction and its magnitude' therefore rests on a false formula; the input transformation only changes the point at which the Jacobian is evaluated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write grad_theta f_i = J_theta h(M^{-1}x)^T grad_z l and explain that M^{-1} enters only through the evaluation point of the Jacobian and the model.
issues.overall_effect: The mechanism by which data-space preconditioning changes the gradient is misstated.
issues.title: Data-space preconditioning gradient formula is incorrect
issues.why_classification: The formula and its interpretation must be re-derived and re-explained, although the section's qualitative message survives.
